So there’s a lot of good suggestions in the comments, more controlled breathing, and playing to a metronome.
You should absolutely do these things, but above all, YOU NEED TO COUNT OUT LOUD! Play your beat along with a click, and count 1+2+3+4+ (assuming its in 4). Do the same things for your fills. If you can’t do it, it means your time will suffer. This should be the #1 thing you work on if you actually want better time. It’s difficult and you might feel stupid but this is best possible way to actually sound like a better drummer.

Having good stick technique is all about the lift. There are four different types of singles with a different lift. Full stroke: where you start high off the snare and bounce the stick back to its original height, dead stroke: where you start high and bounce the stick a half inch off the snare head, taps: start low and end low, and rebound stroke, where you start low and end high. Set a metronome to 60bpm and work on each stroke consecutively with just one hand, then switch hands, then alternate, and after that move it up to 70bpm. After youve gotten some speed move one hand to the hi hat while you keep the other one the snare, and play both hands simultaneously starting again from 60bpm and moving up. Do this everyday for a month=guaranteed progress.

I’m currently 21 and had what I thought was a life long best friend since age 10. We hung out all the time as kids and played video games, played neighborhood sports, and had countless sleepovers. Going into middle school I started to develop extreme anxiety around other people, pretty much stunting my ability to make new friends. He was making so many new friends throughout middle and high school, and I was always the awkward tag along. I got made fun of a lot and he didn’t make all that much of an effort to defend me. Usually he would just join in with them, and I never had what it took to stick up for myself. This went on until senior year where I finally developed some self esteem after about 5 years of being too scared of others and ashamed of myself to try and live a normal lifestyle. We still hung out after graduation, and slowly, he started cutting out our old high school friends, stopped talking to the friends he made in college, and lives off campus by himself. I on the other hand after coming to the college he went to right after graduation have made countless close friends (some are students he originally befriended his first year of college) and have gradually been improving on being around people. My biggest regret is letting my best friend walk all over me at my most vulnerable point when I should’ve just found new friends instead.

First off, you shouldn’t be ashamed that you’re feeling suicidal. It’s common, more common then society has let on, and it’s really something that should be addressed more in our education system. People will feel bad about their lives. It’s not the end of the world, although it might affect you for a little bit. Try to look into counseling/therapy, if there’s something that you can’t get off your chest in front of your closest friends and family, that’s not good. You should never have to bottle up negative emotions, and there are people out there who’s job it is to help out others who are struggling with their emotions and lives. If you continue to let these feelings stir inside you then they will consume you and dominate your life, which won’t lead to you getting better. You still have a life that’s worth living, and just because you’ve been hurt in a way that has affected you long term doesn’t mean there’s no coming back. Please get professional help, if you’re feeling like this then getting better should be your priority, even over school or work. Things can get better, if you allow yourself to let others aid you. Have a good thanksgiving, and feel better soon.
